No Revisit date has passed yet. The next one is **bake-to-order on 2026-12-02**, which falls inside this 30-day window.

## Doubling in 30 days probably isn't realistic

Going from 140 to 280 subscribers means 140 new paying ones by about 19 December. In October you had 15 paid signups. Even a very good push would more likely bring 40–60.

The bigger limit is capacity. Your no-trial record says Saturday slots are already your constraint. If 280 boxes go out on a cargo bike on one Saturday morning, the bread stops arriving warm, and that's the reason you chose your own delivery. So my aim would be **+50 paying subscribers that you can actually deliver**, not +140.

## What I'd do

**Week 1: find your Saturday ceiling**
- Work out how many drops you can make between baking and noon. That number is your real target.
- Add a **Saturday shop pickup** option for pre-ordered boxes. It still fits bake-to-order, uses no delivery slot, and reaches people more than 3 km away.

**Weeks 1–4: subscriber referrals (main lever)**
- Your 140 subscribers are your best channel. Give each one a referral link. The friend gets **50% off their first month**. The subscriber gets a free pastry or an extra loaf for each friend who signs up and pays.
- On 2026-10-06 you discarded 50% off the first month because you expected the same low conversion as the free box. But that record's reopen condition is *"test it with a referral from an existing subscriber"*, so this is that test. Track how many referred signups are still paying in week 5.

**Weeks 2–4: Christmas gift boxes**
- Sell prepaid 4-week gift bread boxes (€72), starting in early January. People already shop for gifts in December. These boxes are paid, don't take December Saturday slots, and give you warm leads to convert.

**Throughout: get denser on your current routes**
- Put door-hangers on streets where you already deliver: "Your neighbour gets our bread every Saturday." Extra stops on those streets cost the bike almost nothing.
- A local social ad shown only within 3 km of the shop, using photos of the bike and warm loaves.

**Budget (~€300):** about €80 for door-hangers and gift cards, about €120 for referral rewards, about €100 for the local ads.

## What I wouldn't do

- **Free trial / free first box.** You discarded it on 2026-10-06: 52 people took a free box and only 6 became paying subscribers. Each box cost about €7 and a Saturday slot. Reopen only if paid signups fall below 8 a month for 2 months in a row. October had 15, so the condition isn't met.
- **Delivery apps or a courier partner to handle more volume.** You discarded both on 2026-08-18. Apps charge 30% commission and cut you off from customers; reopen only if you open a second shop. The cheapest courier quote was €4.50 a drop; reopen only if you pass 300 subscribers.

Once you know your Saturday ceiling and choose which of these to run, I'll log it in the ledger, including the referral test as the reopen trial for the 50% offer.
